LIST OF TORNADO TYPES:
Below is the list of tornadoes that the players can encounter on Tornado Peak.

- TORNADO (gray): An ordinary tornado that tosses any players that get caught in it.

- TALL TORNADO (blue): A taller tornado that tosses players higher than a normal tornado would.

- WIDE TORNADO (green): A wider yet shorter tornado that tosses players farther than a normal tornado would. Particularly risky around the platform's edges.

- ROCKNADO (faded purple): Even though it catches players just like a regular tornado would, this tornado also hurls rocks up in the air. If the rocks land on any players, than those players would get squished. Squished players stick to the ground, which can give them temporary immunity from other tornadoes, but as a drawback, they cannot move.

- ICENADO (light blue): A tornado that keeps a whole ton of ice and snow in its winds. Any players it catches would freeze up, being unable to move until they get caught by another tornado that isn't another icenado. Apart from other tornadoes, players can also be freed from the ice by rocknado rocks.

- CHARGED TORNADO (vibrant purple): Looks like this tornado has fused itself with some lightning! Any players it catches will be tossed WAAAAY high up in the sky. When these players fall down from the sky, they could end up landing on the platform, but they can also end up missing the platform, which can get them KO'd!

Before submitting your remix, check that you've followed all the rules, and make adjustments if necessary:

1. It is HIGHLY suggested to comment "Remixing..." in the comments before starting a remix, so people know not to accidentally split the remix tree's branches. If you don't intend to make a new remix branch, then don't remix if someone has commented "Remixing...". If the queue for remixing the main branch gets too long, you could either wait until later to remix or just make a new remix branch.

2. DO NOT BREAK SCRATCH'S COMMUNITY GUIDELINES!! That means nothing too scary or vulgar & no swear words!

3. Don't delete any of these rules or instructions and don't completely change the project title either!

4. Don't delete or destructively modify anything you didn't make! You are allowed to do this though if something breaks any rules or the Community Guidelines or if you need to fix a bug or glitch.

5. (This rule should only apply to AYs made by ZYellow) Please refrain from adding any content from FNF in the main remix branch. That means no characters, references, AND music tracks from that game. Please respect ZYellow's opinion on this (if you like that game, then he respects your opinion).

6. Don't delete any music tracks unless they break the Community Guidelines. If you don't want to listen to a certain song or genre, utilize the "audio exemption" functionality to make sure you can't.

7. On the topic of music, please also refer to the Music comment's recommended music limit so that it can't have too much lag from this project.

8. You can add yourself to the thumbnail, but please don't delete any characters off it or completely change it altogether!

!!=`TR~(1OY{u^Ng(8z3.text:
Change all the "voice" sound clips to your own character's voice! If your character doesn't have a voice, you can either mute the voice-clips, and potentially add a cheering audience for their Win!Voice, or make them any non-vocal noises the character makes.

VOICE-CLIP GUIDE:
Caught: You can add as many of these as you want, though if you do, the caught voice count in the block above should match how many caught voices you actually have in your player sprite. This sound plays when the player is caught inside of a tornado, and is Tornado Peak's equivalent to an ouch voice clip.

Stunned: A muffled ouch-like voice that plays when a player is frozen, squished, or making a hard land after falling from being launched by a charged tornado.

Shocked: A scared cry reacting to getting intensely launched upwards by a charged tornado.

KO!: Screaming & shouting as they fall off the platform!

Win!: The character's victory phrase for when they outlast all the others and win the game!

//xf(mVju:mbK3`GOzLX.text:
If you want to add your own music loops...

1) Separate your song into it's intro (if it has an intro) and the section that loops. (if you're looping a music track that originally doesn't loop, you may also save the end section in it's own sound for another time)

2) Tag '-Start' at the end of the intro's name, and tag '-Loop' onto the looping part's name too.

3) Add the song's name into the 'Add music' block that matches which scenario it's for, and drop it here.

Remember that the song name must always be spelt the same, or else the loop won't work! If you're unsure, test it.

If the music track or jingle comes from a party game, like Mario Party, Wii Party or WarioWare: MEGA Party Game$, make sure it won't play for users who don't want those music tracks, like SmashBrosFan2020, via the audio-exemption lists & Boolean. Same goes for "gets faster" tracks, music from Miitopia, music from Flash/HTML5 games, music from Lunar Pool, lyrical music, non-looping music, and music from Mario Kart 8 Deluxe's DLC.

I also recommend you please don't add any more than around 100 music tracks and jingles total, to prevent lag or the dreaded "refusal-to-save glitch" when modifying the project on less powerful devices. It's also best to refrain from adding too many music tracks longer than 3 minutes (180 seconds) or too many "gets faster" tracks.
